reason: E1 confirms active screen nitriding of TC4 improves hardness and wear resistance, but does not specify the exact phase structure, hardness multiplier, or friction reduction claimed. E2 confirms the graded δ-TiN/ϵ-Ti2N + α-Ti(N) structure and strong hardening for PBII nitriding, but uses a different process (PBII, not active screen) and does not quantify friction reduction. The specific quantitative outcomes and the seamless bonding premise are thus only partially supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Active screen ion nitriding of TC4 at ~550°C produces a graded nitride layer with outer δ-TiN/ϵ-Ti2N and inner α-Ti(N).
Such a layer increases surface hardness by 2–3× relative to untreated TC4 (~310 HV).
Such a layer reduces friction coefficient by ~20–30% relative to untreated TC4.
The process yields a seamless metallurgical bond to the substrate.
